jobs.title: Business Development Representative
jobs.location: Northern America, Europe, UK, France, European timezones
jobs.jd_full:
## About Outsite

 

Outsite is a global coliving company for remote workers — hotel-quality service, extended-stay flexibility, and a built-in community, at the intersection of hospitality and lifestyle. We operate 40+ properties across 21+ cities on 5 continents, with 6,000+ verified members and an NPS of 65.

 

## About Outsite for Teams

 

Outsite for Teams is Outsite's B2B expansion — giving companies, teams, and communities access to our global network of coliving and coworking spaces for their employees. Rather than a bulk discount, we position it as a meaningful perk: founders and leaders purchase memberships on behalf of their team, and a dedicated account manager keeps them active and engaged. This is a genuine growth priority for the business, and you'll be one of the first dedicated sales hires driving it.

 

## Role Overview

 

We're hiring a Business Development Representative to build and run outbound sales for Outsite for Teams. You'll identify and prospect the right companies, run discovery calls, and close new business — turning remote-first startups, distributed teams, and growth-stage companies into long-term Outsite for Teams accounts.

 

This is a highly autonomous, build-it-yourself role. You'll help shape the outbound playbook, not just execute someone else's.

 

## Key Responsibilities

 

### 1. Prospecting & Outbound

- Build and work target lists of remote-first and hybrid companies, using signals like team size (50–500), remote/hybrid language in company descriptions, and titles such as Head of People, Chief of Staff, VP of Operations, or Founder

- Source leads via LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Wellfound/AngelList, Crunchbase, remote job boards (We Work Remotely, Remote.co), and Outsite's own member base

- Run cold outbound via email, LinkedIn, and calls, and continuously test and refine messaging

- Reach out to local companies near Outsite locations to sell business travel and corporate stay packages

- Build partnerships with travel agencies and tour operators to generate referral and bundled-stay opportunities

 

### 2. Sales & Pipeline Management

- Run discovery calls to understand a prospect's team, travel patterns, and remote work culture

- Own the full sales cycle from first touch to close

- Keep the CRM clean and current — every deal staged, every next step logged

- Forecast pipeline accurately and hit monthly/quarterly new business targets

 

### 3. Collaboration & Handoff

- Partner with the Head of Marketing on positioning, collateral, and campaigns that support outbound

- Hand off closed accounts cleanly to the account management side, with full context on the client's goals

- Share market feedback — what's resonating, what isn't — to sharpen Outsite for Teams' pitch and ICP over time

 

### 4. Reporting

- Report weekly on pipeline: volume, stage, conversion, and blockers

- Track and share what's working in outbound so it can be systematized

 

## Required Skills & Experience

 

- 1+ years of B2B sales or business development experience (SDR/BDR background a plus)

- Confident, consultative communicator — comfortable running discovery calls with founders and People leaders

- Self-starter who's built pipeline from scratch, not just worked warm leads

- Able to work autonomously and independently 

- Comfortable with taking initiative and being proactive 

- Comfortable working European timezone hours

- Strong written communication — outbound copy is part of the job

- Organized; keeps a CRM honest without being told to

- Comfortable using AI in workflow

 

## Nice to Have

 

- Experience selling to remote-first or distributed teams

- Familiarity with Pipedrive or HubSpot

- Existing network in the startup, remote work, or travel/hospitality space

- Experience selling a membership, subscription, or perk-style product

 

## What Success Looks Like (First 90 Days)

 

- A working, documented outbound playbook (lists, messaging, cadence)

- A full and accurately-staged pipeline in the CRM

- First qualified meetings booked and first deals in late-stage or closed

- Clear, weekly reporting rhythm established with Marketing

- Sharpened point of view on which ICPs convert fastest

 

## Benefits

 

- Remote, travel encouraged

- Credits for Outsite locations 

- Salary - $45,000 - $50,000 USD + commission

This role is integral to enabling Liberty Mutual's ability to bring policy forms to market quickly and accurately while supporting regulatory compliance, profitability programs, and platform convergence initiatives. Join a team at the center of how Liberty Mutual brings insurance products to market. You'll own the delivery of policy form content that directly impacts profitability, regulatory compliance, and customer experience — while shaping a modernizing forms ecosystem undergoing significant convergence and operating model evolution. If you thrive on balancing speed, quality, and stakeholder complexity in a high-throughput environment, this is your role.

  • Background working with form template technologies (e.g., LibreOffice, open-source document generation tools, or similar)
  • Experience managing vendor/contractor delivery

Responsibilities

Participates in PI Planning ceremonies and sets sprint/PI-level priorities in alignment with ECS OKRs, USRM business priorities, and forms analyst filing timelines

jobs.title: Technical Product Owner - Core Services
jobs.jd_full:
Location
Our Technical Product Owner - DoiT Cloud Intelligence - Core Services will be an integral part of our global Product team. This role is based remotely in the East Coast US, the UK, Ireland, Estonia, the Netherlands, Sweden and Israel.

Who We Are
DoiT is a global technology company that works with cloud-driven organizations to leverage the cloud to drive business growth and innovation. We combine data, technology, and human expertise to ensure our customers operate in a well-architected and scalable state - from planning to production. Delivering DoiT Cloud Intelligence, the only solution that integrates advanced technology with human intelligence, we help our customers solve complex multi-cloud problems and drive efficiency. With decades of multi-cloud experience, we have specializations in Kubernetes, GenAI, CloudOps, and more. An award-winning strategic partner of AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, we work alongside more than 4,000 customers worldwide.

The OpportunityWe’re hiring a Technical Product Owner to drive rapid delivery and iteration for the Core Services team of DoiT Cloud Intelligence, our platform that helps DevOps, Cloud Infrastructure, and FinOps teams manage public cloud environments effectively and efficiently. Core Services builds and operates foundational platform capabilities used across DoiT’s products and engineering teams. Its responsibilities include identity and access management, authentication and authorization, customer and tenant services, shared APIs, platform integrations, and other cross-cutting capabilities. This role is designed for someone with a technical product mindset who is comfortable working deep within platform architecture, distributed systems, APIs, cloud infrastructure, and internal engineering workflows. You will help turn broad platform needs into clear technical product direction, sequenced investments, and reliably delivered capabilities. You will report to a VP of Product and work as an embedded member of the Core Services Engineering team. You will collaborate closely with engineering leadership, architects, security, product teams, and internal platform consumers to determine what the team should build next and why.

Role clarity: VP of Product vs. Technical Product Owner

VP of Product (what they own)

  • Sets the overall vision, strategy, positioning, and long-range roadmap for the platform area.
  • Makes the highest-level prioritization calls across multiple components and investment themes.
  • Aligns stakeholders across the company (executive leadership, GTM, partners) on direction and tradeoffs.
  • Defines success at the portfolio/area level and ensures the area’s outcomes ladder up to company goals.

Technical Product Owner (what you own)

  • Owns delivery, iteration, and learning velocity for the Core Services.
  • Turns VP-level direction into clear problems to solve, a prioritized backlog, and incrementally shippable scope.
  • Runs the feedback loop: discover → define → build → release → measure → iterate, repeatedly.
  • Works within the Engineering teams to ensure they are always building the highest-value next increment with clarity, quality
  • Review technical designs, reason about tradeoffs and constraints, and understand their impact on delivery timelines and system behavior, without being the primary implementer
  • Leverages deep, hands-on DevOps experience and public cloud understanding to ensure that solution implementations are done correctly

This distinction matters: the VP creates the “why” and “where”; the Product Owner ensures the “what next” is always sharp, validated, and shipping.

Responsibilities

Fast iteration and backlog leadership

  • Translate the VP’s strategy into a sequenced backlog of problems, user stories, and acceptance criteria that the Engineering team can deliver continuously.
  • Keep work “thin-sliced” so the team can ship frequently, learn quickly, and reduce risk through iteration.
  • Maintain a disciplined cadence of backlog refinement, sprint readiness, and scope negotiation to keep delivery predictable without slowing innovation.

Deep user and workflow understanding

  • Leverage your hands-on DevOps experience and expertise in the real-world workflows of the professionals you’re building for - especially cloud operators and practitioners.
  • Use firsthand domain knowledge and ongoing customer conversations to identify friction, gaps, and opportunities for differentiation.
  • Prioritize enhancements that materially improve outcomes: speed, reliability, clarity, safety, governance, cost impact, or operational simplicity.

Customer validation and external communication

  • Often speak with customers (aiming for 3-5 calls a week) and cross-functional DoiT stakeholders regularly to test ideas, validate assumptions, and pressure-test tradeoffs.
  • Communicate clearly and confidently: share concepts early, take feedback openly, synthesize input into decisions, and explain “why” in a way that builds trust.
  • Rely on your hands-on, DevOps experience to go deep with stakeholders (internal/external) into the technical details of the problem, our solution, and the contexts and environments in which both of these exist.
  • Support beta/design-partner motions where appropriate by shaping hypotheses, success criteria, and rollout plans.

Engineering-embedded technical product ownership

  • Operate as a core member of the Core Services’ Engineering team - present in daily collaboration, crisp in decision-making, and pragmatic about constraints.
  • Partner with Engineering leads on sequencing, technical tradeoffs, and delivery planning - ensuring product intent survives implementation realities.
  • Ensure Core Services are cohesive across UX, APIs, data, and operational behavior - and that it meets a high bar for reliability and customer trust.

Quality, outcomes, and measurement

  • Define what “success” means for Core Services with clear metrics (adoption, activation, workflow completion, time-to-value, retention, reliability signals, customer-reported impact).
  • Instrument learning: make sure releases are measurable and that insights reliably flow back into prioritization.
  • Own release readiness for Core Services: documentation, enablement inputs, and clear communication of what’s new and why it matters.

Safety, governance, and trust by design

  • Ensure product requirements account for real-world cloud environments: IAM boundaries, auditability, guardrails, and safe defaults.
  • Partner with security, support, and customer teams to anticipate edge cases and ensure Core Services earns trust over time.

Qualifications

  • 7–10 years of hands-on experience as a Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, SRE, Cloud Engineer, Solutions Architect, or a similar roles working with or building products for public cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, and/or Azure).
  • A strong product sense for turning messy problems into clear scope and shipped value - without waiting for perfect information.
  • Systems thinking: Ability to reason about complex distributed systems, architectural tradeoffs, and long-term platform evolution.
  • Prioritization: Demonstrated ability to balance customer needs, engineering constraints, and platform investments when making prioritization decisions.
  • Deep curiosity and technical fluency in cloud fundamentals (cost/billing concepts, identity/IAM, networking, compute, Kubernetes, observability, automation), and experience building solutions that leverage or focus on these technologies
  • Coding experience is a plus - enough to collaborate effectively with engineers, reason about feasibility, and understand system behaviors.
  • Excellent communication skills: you can explain complex ideas simply, facilitate alignment, and confidently engage with customers and experts.
  • A bias for action and continuous improvement: you ship, measure, learn, and iterate - building capabilities that become a meaningful competitive differentiator.

How success will be measured

  • The Core Services’ roadmap advances through frequent, high-quality releases with clear customer value.
  • Customer feedback loops are strong: you can show how insights translated into shipped improvements.
  • Adoption and outcomes improve measurably (usage, engagement, workflow completion, reliability, and customer impact).
  • The Engineering team consistently has clarity on the next most valuable increment to build - and why.

We are home to a global team of incredible talent who work remotely and have the flexibility to have a schedule that balances your work and home life. We embrace and support leveling up your skills professionally and personally.

We thought so too, but we’re here and happy we hit that ‘apply’ button.

About Limble

At Limble we empower the unsung heroes who support the world. We’re revolutionizing the way businesses manage their maintenance operations by providing a comprehensive suite of software solutions that empower organizations to optimize asset performance and drive operational excellence. From preventive maintenance to inventory management and beyond, our robust CMMS platform offers a suite of features designed to streamline operations and enhance productivity.

About the Role

AI is a growing part of how we build our product and how our team works. We’re exploring how AI and machine learning can help maintenance teams predict equipment failures before they happen, catch problems earlier, and prevent costly downtime, and more. Within your product area, you’ll help shape where AI creates the most value for our customers, while also using it to move faster in your own day-to-day. You’ll report to a Group Product Manager, most likely on our Inventory Management product, though your specific product area may shift based on business needs.

How you’ll make an impact

  • Gathering, organizing, and prioritizing feature requests and requirements from customers, sales, design, and other stakeholders

  • Writing clear product requirements and driving timely cross-functional execution

Requirements

  • Experience working in an Agile development environment and product management tools (e.g., Productboard, JIRA), including building roadmaps and communicating updates to stakeholders

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
About the Role

Conversica is looking for a Senior Product Manager to help shape the next generation of our AI-powered products. This role sits at the intersection of customers, engineering, sales, and customer success, translating customer and market needs into clear product direction and solutions that create measurable business impact.

Working closely with the Chief Product Officer, you will lead product discovery, help define new product capabilities, partner with Engineering throughout the development lifecycle, and support the successful introduction of new products and features to the market.

This is an opportunity to influence the future direction of Conversica’s product portfolio and contribute across the full product lifecycle, from customer discovery and product definition through launch and adoption.

What You’ll Do

Product Strategy and Discovery

  • Conduct customer discovery interviews and market research to identify customer needs, pain points, and market opportunities.

  • Help shape product strategy and priorities in alignment with company objectives.

  • Translate customer and market insights into clear product requirements, functional specifications, and user stories.

  • Prioritize product initiatives based on customer value, business impact, strategic alignment, and technical feasibility.

  • Bring customer insights and market perspectives into roadmap and product-planning discussions.

Product Development

  • Partner closely with Engineering throughout the product development lifecycle.

  • Provide clear context, requirements, and success criteria for new product capabilities.

  • Work through product questions and tradeoffs with technical and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Drive alignment across Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success.

  • Support roadmap planning, feature prioritization, and product decision-making.

Go-to-Market and Product Marketing

  • Develop clear product positioning, messaging, and value propositions.

  • Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing to plan and execute product launches.

  • Create sales enablement materials, competitive insights, and internal product education.

  • Ensure customer-facing teams understand new product capabilities, their intended value, and how to position them effectively.

  • Contribute product content and product demonstrations to support launches and customer education.

  • Gather feedback following launches to inform adoption efforts and future product improvements.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Serve as a strong voice of the customer across the organization.

  • Build trusted relationships with Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and executive leadership.

  • Influence product decisions through customer feedback, market knowledge, business context, and data.

  • Communicate product direction and decisions clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.

Success in This Role

Within your first 6 to 12 months, you will:

  • Establish a consistent approach to customer discovery and synthesizing customer insights.

  • Become a trusted partner to Engineering and cross-functional stakeholders.

  • Strengthen product requirements, product definition, and decision-making practices.

  • Help prioritize the roadmap based on customer needs, company strategy, and business impact.

  • Improve cross-functional readiness and alignment for new product launches.

  • Bring meaningful customer and market insights into strategic product discussions.

  • Help drive stronger understanding, adoption, and feedback for newly launched capabilities.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of product management experience in a B2B SaaS environment.

  • Experience owning products or major product initiatives from customer discovery through launch.

  • Strong experience partnering closely with Engineering teams.

  • Demonstrated ability to gather customer insights and translate them into clear product requirements and decisions.

  • Experience writing product requirements, functional specifications, user stories, or similar product documentation.

  • Experience contributing to product positioning, launches, or other outbound product activities.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Experience working cross-functionally with Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and product leadership.

  • Ability to operate independently and effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.jd_full:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

We are hiring a Staff Product Manager for self-serve. You will own the growth of the developer’s journey from first touch to committed customer — as much of that funnel as the team’s size calls for — and you will build the product that moves it. This is a founding-era team: the systems are young, the questions are not handed to you, and the person in this role defines what good looks like rather than executing someone else’s definition. You report to the VP of Self-Serve and partner daily with engineering, design, developer relations, and the product analyst who owns the measurement behind your work.

What You’ll Do

- The growth of the self-serve funnel — the metrics, the experiments that move them, and the product changes behind them. Your span may be one part of the funnel or the whole of it, and it can grow or narrow as the team does.

- The product across that experience — onboarding, the console, and the activation path a developer travels. You decide what ships and why; engineering builds it, and the developer-experience team owns the SDKs and docs you build on.

- The complete system your area runs on, stood up from scratch: the rhythms of business, data-driven optimization, and the experimentation platform. You build it yourself or in-house, or you research and deploy the best tools available.

- A weekly rhythm of shipping and measuring: a hypothesis, a change, an honest read of whether it worked, and the next bet. Not a roadmap of features shipped on faith.

- The cross-team work that falls between owners: with developer relations on acquisition and the shared developer platforms, with marketing on search and answer-engine presence, with sales and customer success on the handoff, and with the analyst on definitions and instrumentation.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Student Loans Marketplace
jobs.jd_full:
Who is Credible?

Credible is a leading U.S. consumer finance marketplace, transforming the way consumers access and compare financial products. We operate at a consumer and enterprise level. On the consumer side, we help millions of people make smarter financial decisions by comparing personalized, pre-qualified offers across student loans, personal loans, mortgages, credit cards, and insurance — all without impacting their credit score. On the enterprise side, we power financial product comparison and distribution through deep integrations and partnerships with lenders, insurance carriers, and financial institutions, as well as providing marketplace technology and capabilities to third-party partners and distribution channels.

About the Role:

Credible is looking for an AI-native Senior Product Manager to take ownership of our student loan lending marketplace, our flagship product. You will own and deliver features from ideation through launch, in close collaboration with design, engineering, and data. Primarily, you’ll focus on the front-end experience that helps students and parents discover and compare options across multiple lenders.

This role requires AI fluency in both how you work and what you build. In your workflow, you bring working concepts rather than documents describing them, using AI tools like Claude to prototype ideas, run your own analysis, and validate concepts before committing engineering resources. You bring the experience and rigor to know which few ideas are worth building, and the drive to see them through.

In the product itself, you will shape how Credible reaches users as loan discovery moves beyond the comparison page and into AI assistants and embedded experiences, and you will determine where AI belongs within our own funnel to make comparing and choosing a loan simpler. Where AI touches the product, you own the quality bar: defining what good output looks like, measuring it, and ensuring it stays accurate and compliant.

Teams will look to you and your product leadership to guide the product’s vision and direction and to achieve team OKRs.

Responsibilities:

  • Think Strategically and Creatively: Deliver new features for growing the student loan marketplace and align them with Credible’s long-term vision. Synthesize market trends, regulatory shifts in the student loan space, user needs, and rapidly advancing AI capabilities to continually reinvent the platform, including how it reaches users beyond our own site.
  • Own AI-Powered Product Surfaces: Shape how Credible helps students and parents discover and choose loans through AI assistants, embedded experiences, and AI-assisted flows within our own funnel. Decide where AI meaningfully improves the experience and where it doesn’t belong.
  • Own the Roadmap: Manage roadmaps for both private student loans and student loan refinance products by identifying opportunities, weighing tradeoffs, and prioritizing team resources. Decide not only what to build, but what to remove when it isn’t earning its place.
  • Prototype and Validate: Use AI tools like Claude to build working concepts, test them quickly, and validate ideas with real artifacts. Explore many approaches, and find the ones that resonate with users and lenders.
  • Make Data-Driven Decisions: Utilize data analysis, A/B testing, and user research to validate assumptions, uncover insights, and drive meaningful improvements to the business. Run your own queries and analysis rather than depending on others for every question.
  • Lead and Collaborate Across Functions: Proactively engage cross-functional teams to brainstorm innovative solutions and lead their implementation. Collaborate with engineering, design, data, partnerships, and operations teams to deliver product enhancements and achieve team OKRs.
  • Operate Responsibly in a Regulated Space: Student lending is compliance-constrained. Understand where AI-assisted work and AI-generated output need human review, where claims and disclosures matter, and how to move fast without creating regulatory or trust risk.

Education and Experience:

  • At least 4 years of experience in a Product Management role for web-based consumer Internet products
  • Bachelor’s Degree
  • Deep, demonstrated fluency using AI tools in your actual workflow for prototyping, analysis, research synthesis, and writing, with a clear point of view on where they help and where they don’t
  • Genuine interest in and ideas about building AI-powered product experiences, not just using AI to work faster
  • Ability to bring working concepts to life, whether through AI tooling, light coding, or strong partnership with engineering
  • Familiarity with how to evaluate AI output quality, or clear aptitude and appetite to own it
  • Ability to use data, your experience, and product instincts to identify the most impactful areas of focus, including running your own analysis
  • Strong analytical abilities across spreadsheets, SQL, and other analytics tools
  • Exceptional problem-solving and communication skills
  • Strong project management skills, and willingness/ability to own critical parts of the product, end-to-end
  • Thrive on collaboration with other teams to accomplish shared goals
  • Technical aptitude sufficient to work closely with engineers, evaluate implementation approaches, and weigh cost/benefit tradeoffs
  • A bias toward experimentation and the discipline to walk away from your own ideas when the evidence says so

Pursuant to state and local pay disclosure requirements, the pay ranges for this role, with final offer amount dependent on education, skills, experience, and location, are listed below. This role is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, various benefits, including medical/dental/vision, insurance, a 401(k) plan, paid time off, and other benefits in accordance with applicable plan documents.

View more details about Credible Benefits

$128,000—$149,000 USD

For all other US locations:

$111,000—$136,000 USD

Why work at Credible?

We combine the intelligence, expertise, and confidence of a financial advisor with the approachability and honesty of a friend. In other words, we’re the friend you always wish you had in finance.

We are optimistic, challengers, trustworthy, clever, and smart. We are open and transparent. We strive to act as advisors by being friendly, objective, and open in our communication. We use language that is intelligent yet approachable. When appropriate, we’ll drop in a bit of wit to position ourselves as a fresh, reliable voice in the financial world.
